example.caption: The OKS query language itself: scope tokens, comparators, boolean operators, relationship quantifiers and path-query syntax. The BNF is reconstructed; the authoritative sources are src/query.cpp and include/oks/query.hpp, quoted in docs/OKS_Grammar_Query_CppAPI_Reference.pdf.
example.query-grammar:
query ::= "(" scope expr ")" scope ::= "this" | "all" ; this = class only, all = class + subclasses expr ::= attr_cmp | uid_cmp | rel_expr | and_expr | or_expr | not_expr and_expr ::= "and" expr expr+ ; two or more operands or_expr ::= "or" expr expr+ ; two or more operands not_expr ::= "not" expr ; exactly one operand attr_cmp ::= "(" "\"attr-name\"" "\"value\"" op ")" uid_cmp ::= "(" "object-id" "\"an-object-id\"" "=" ")" rel_expr ::= "(" "\"rel-name\"" ("some"|"all") expr ")" path_query ::= "(" "path-to" "\"dest-id@class\"" path_expr ")" path_expr ::= "(" ("direct"|"nested") "\"rel-name\""+ path_expr? ")" op ::= "=" | "!=" | "~=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">="
Notes grounded in src/query.cpp and include/oks/query.hpp: * the first token of a query must be 'all' or 'this'; anything else fails to parse * 'all' is overloaded: class scope at the top level, universal quantifier inside a relationship expression * '~=' is boost::regex_match, so the pattern must match the whole value; there is no glob operator * object-id supports '=' only * a value is always written as a quoted token; the attribute's declared type decides whether the comparison is numeric, boolean or lexicographic * a nested relationship expression is parsed against the relationship's class-type, not against the outer class

example.caption: ROD busy module. Defines 3 class(es): BusyChannel, BusyTimeoutAction, RODBusyModule. [Source: test_schema/xml/RODBusy.schema.xml]
example.schema-file:
<oks-schema> <info name="" type="" num-of-items="3" oks-format="schema" oks-version="oks-06-10-01 built "Mar 16 2016"" created-by="pedro" created-on="lxplus073" creation-time="20040303T105404" last-modified-by="pauly" last-modified-on="pcphate20.cern.ch" last-modification-time="20160510T124956" /> <include> <file path="daq/schema/df.schema.xml" /> </include> <class name="BusyChannel" description="Busy channel with a relationship to a ResourceBase.
Id corresponds to a busy channel number (0-15 for RODBusyModule; 0-2 for LTP, 0-4 for CTPOUT, etc): the channel number where the busy cable is plugged into.
The ResourceBase should be the corresponding Resource where the busy is formed. Depending on the Resource, the BusyChannel can be taken into account or ignored.
Examples:
- ROD for a RODBusy channel
- RODBusyModule for a RODBusyModule (the busy that goes out of the RODBusy comes from itself, from the internal OR of its busy channels)
- RCDLTPModule for RCDLTPModule (similar to RODBusyModule)
- if no resource is available in the database, an ad-hoc Resource can be created. By putting it into the Resources relationship of a segment, one can enable/disable it conveniently.
" is-abstract="no"> <superclass name="Resource" /> <attribute name="Id" description="Id of busy channel: can have different meaning, 
typically the channel number of the module where 
this BusyChannel is plugged into." type="u32" init-value="0" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="BusyTimeout" description="Number of seconds this busy channel is allowed to stay busy at 100%, before its ResourceBase gets automatically disabled.
The special case of "0" means that no timeout is used." type="u32" init-value="0" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="RecoveryTimeout" description="Number of seconds this busy channel is allowed to stay busy before a recovery attempt is performed.
The special case of "0" means that no timeout is used." type="u32" init-value="0" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" /> <relationship name="BusySource" description="Relationship to the ResourceBase, which provides the busy signal." class-type="ResourceBase" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> </class> <class name="BusyTimeoutAction" description="Base class for the action to be performed in caso of a busy timeout or recovery timeout." is-abstract="yes"> </class> <class name="RODBusyModule" description="Plugin for ReadoutApplication for the RODBusy VME board. Each busy channel (class BusyChannel) can be linked to the relationship Contains." is-abstract="no"> <superclass name="ReadoutModule" /> <superclass name="ResourceSet" /> <superclass name="BusyChannel" /> <attribute name="TimeoutFraction" description="Timeout busy fraction threshold: if the busy fraction stays above this threshold, the timeout
watchdog will count it as being above threshold." type="double" init-value="1.0" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="useConfiguration" description="Configure the RODBusy according to the oks database" type="bool" init-value="true" is-not-null="yes" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" /> <attribute name="MonitoringLevel" description="Sets the level of monitoring to be performed on a RODBusy module." type="enum" range="None,Basic,Detailed" init-value="None" is-not-null="yes" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" /> <attribute name="IS_ServerName" description="IS server name used for RODBusy Monitoring" type="string" init-value="Monitoring" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="IS_UpdatePeriod" description="Period (in seconds) of regular updates for basic and detailed monitoring" type="u16" range="1..30" init-value="5" is-not-null="yes" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" /> <attribute name="ServiceRequest_Limit" description="Maximum number of counts of the limit counter (100ns intervals of busy, LIMREG register) within the reset period (attribute ServiceRequest_ResetPeriod), at which point a service request is generated." type="u16" range="0..65535" init-value="65535" is-not-null="yes" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" /> <attribute name="ServiceRequest_ResetPeriod" description="Number of 10MHz clock ticks (100ns, IVALREG register) which resets the limit counter." type="u16" range="0..65535" init-value="0" is-not-null="yes" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" /> <attribute name="EmulateVME" description="For debugging only. If true(=1), all vme access is skipped and the IS entries are filled with mock data. *** NOT YET IMPLEMENTED ***" type="bool" init-value="false" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" /> <relationship name="BusyRecoveryAction" description="Link to a BusyTimeoutAction plugin which performs
user-defined actions when a recovery is requested." class-type="BusyTimeoutAction" low-cc="zero" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="BusyTimeoutAction" description="Link to a BusyTimeoutAction to be performed when
a busy channel has to be removed having hit the
large busy timeout." class-type="BusyTimeoutAction" low-cc="zero" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> </class> </oks-schema>

example.caption: TDAQ core: partitions, segments, applications, computers, software repositories, tags and resources. Every other schema builds on it. Defines 83 class(es): Application, BaseApplication, Binary, BinaryFile, Cable, Component, Computer, ComputerBase, ComputerProgram, ComputerSet, ConnectorCable, Crate, and 71 more. <oks-schema> <info name="" type="" num-of-items="3" oks-format="schema" oks-version="oks-08-03-02-14-g572fc09 built "Mar 11 2021"" created-by="vandelli" created-on="lxplus007.cern.ch" creation-time="20050606T114308" last-modified-by="isolov" last-modified-on="pcatd79.cern.ch" last-modification-time="20210312T111813" /> <class name="SamplingAddress" description="Defines sampling address for event monitoring" is-abstract="yes"> <attribute name="SamplerType" type="string" is-not-null="yes" description="" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" init-value="" ordered="no" /> <attribute name="SamplerNames" description="Monitoring task will be connected to all samplers

If SamplerNames list is empty then the monitoring task will be connected to the given number
of arbitrary chosen samplers of the SamplerType type." type="u16" init-value="1" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" ordered="no" /> </class> <class name="SamplingParameters" description="Defines all necessary parameters for event monitoring" is-abstract="no"> <superclass name="SamplingAddress" /> <superclass name="SelectionCriteria" /> <attribute name="BufferSize" description="Size of the buffer to store events locally. It should be small (<10) if full
event are sampled. In case of sampling from ROD or ROS it should be made 
bigger (e.g. 1000) to have the best sampling performance." type="u32" init-value="100" is-not-null="yes" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" ordered="no" /> <attribute name="GroupName" description="Name of the monitoring group. Monitors with the same group name and
selection criteria will never receive same events. This attribute replaces functionality of DispersalDistribution: 
if GroupName is non-empty, dispersion is set to true" type="string" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" init-value="" is-not-null="no" ordered="no" /> </class> <class name="SelectionCriteria" description="Defines selection criteria for event monitoring" is-abstract="yes"> <attribute name="L1TriggerType" description="LVL1 trigger type" type="u8" format="hex" init-value="0" range="" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" ordered="no" /> <attribute name="L1TriggerType_Ignore" description="If the value is non zero then L1TriggerType 
value will not be used for event selection." type="bool" init-value="1" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" ordered="no" /> <attribute name="L1Bits" description="List of positions of non-zero bits in the L1 information. Interpretation
of these bits depends on the value of the L1BitPattern_Logic parameter." type="u16" is-multi-value="yes" range="" format="dec" init-value="" is-not-null="no" ordered="no" /> <attribute name="L1Bits_Logic" description="If the value is IGNORE then L1Bits value will not be used for event selection.
Value AND means that all bits given by L1Bits have to be present in event header, 
OR requires at least one of them to be set in event header to get this event selected." type="enum" range="IGNORE,AND,OR" init-value="IGNORE" is-not-null="yes" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" ordered="no" /> <attribute name="L1Bits_Origin" description="Defines which of the three L1 bit sets existed in an event header have to be matched." type="enum" range="BEFORE_PRESCALE,AFTER_PRESCALE,AFTER_VETO" init-value="AFTER_VETO" is-not-null="yes" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" ordered="no" /> <attribute name="StatusWord" description="Event header status word. Selection will succeed if at least 
one status word in event header is the same as this one." type="u32" format="hex" init-value="0" range="" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" ordered="no" /> <attribute name="StatusWord_Ignore" description="If the value is non zero then StatusWord
will not be used for event selection." type="bool" init-value="1" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" ordered="no" /> <attribute name="StreamType" description="Event stream type name." type="string" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" init-value="" is-not-null="no" ordered="no" /> <attribute name="StreamNames" description="List of event streams names. List can be empty in which case
all events of the given StreamType will be selected." type="string" is-multi-value="yes" range="" format="dec" init-value="" is-not-null="no" ordered="no" /> <attribute name="Stream_Logic" description="Value IGNORE excludes StreamType and StreamNames from being used for selection.

Note that if nROBDistribution and Subdetector both evaluates to zero, no ROBs are selected." is-abstract="no"> <attribute name="subDetector" description="If this value is 0) ROBs from all available SubDetectors (eformat::FULL_SD_EVENT) are selected. 1) in the range [1..0xf] ROBs from this subDetectorGroup are selected. 2) in the range [0x10..0xff] ROBs from this subDetector are selected. " type="u8" format="hex" init-value="0" range="" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="nROBDistribution" description="This attribute determines the number of ROB's to be requested. What ROBs can be selected depends on the setting of the subDetector attribute. The value for nROBDistribution can be configured to be constant, a Root function or a Root histogram, see class dccommon::Distribution. " type="string" init-value="C|1" is-not-null="yes" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" /> <attribute name="comment" description="Optional description of this data access." type="string" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" init-value="" is-not-null="no" /> </class> <class name="DummyCalStreamTag" description="Specifies optional calibration data that can be produced by this step." is-abstract="no"> <superclass name="DummyStreamTag" /> <attribute name="comment" description="Optional description of this stream tag." type="string" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" init-value="" is-not-null="no" /> <relationship name="calibData" description="The calibration data (ROBs) that will be produced if this tag is activated. " class-type="DataAccess" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" multi-value-implementation="list" /> </class> <class name="DummyROBStep" description="An algorithm step that asks for ROI data and burns cpu time." is-abstract="no"> <superclass name="DummyStep" /> <relationship name="roi" description="The ROBs to be collected for this algorithm step." class-type="DataAccess" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" multi-value-implementation="list" /> </class> <class name="DummyStep" description="An algorithm using the full event data and burns cpu time." is-abstract="no"> <attribute name="burnTimeDistribution" description="Burn time distribution in micro seconds for this step. The burn time values can be configured to be constant, a Root function or a Root histogram, see class dccommon::Distribution." type="string" init-value="C|0" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="comment" description="Optional description of this algorithm step." type="string" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" init-value="" is-not-null="no" /> <relationship name="physicsTag" description="The probability that this step accepts the event." class-type="DummyStreamTag" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" multi-value-implementation="list" /> <relationship name="debugTag" description="The probability that this step sends this event to the DEBUG stream." class-type="DummyStreamTag" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" multi-value-implementation="list" /> <relationship name="calibrationTag" description="The calibration data produced by this step." class-type="DummyCalStreamTag" low-cc="zero" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" multi-value-implementation="list" /> </class> <class name="DummyStreamTag" description="Configuration for a stream tag that can be applied by the dummy steering." is-abstract="no"> <attribute name="name" description="The name of the stream tag" type="string" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" init-value="" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="probability" description="The probability that this StreamTag will take effect." type="float" range="0.0..1.0" init-value="0.0" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="comment" description="Description of this stream tag." type="string" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" init-value="" is-not-null="no" /> </class> <class name="PuDummySteering" description="The PuDummySteering is a dummy implementation of the hltinterface. It is used to emulate the PESA Steering processing when the PESA Steering is not available or not desired. The PuDummy steering defines a set of algorithms that that are executed sequentially until an algorithm rejects the event or all steps have accepted the event. " is-abstract="no"> <superclass name="HLTImplementation" /> <attribute name="resultSizeDistribution" description="Size in 32 bit words of the HLT result. The result size values can be configured to be constant, a Root function or the value from a Root histogram, see class dccommon::Distribution." type="string" init-value="C|1000" is-not-null="yes" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" /> <attribute name="nbrHltTriggerInfo" description="Number of HLT trigger info words." type="u8" init-value="0" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="nbrPscErrors" description="Number of PSC error words" type="u8" init-value="0" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="seed" description="This value is used to indirectly seed both std::rand and Root global grandom. If seed is 1) less than zero the PID is used as a seed. 2) greater than zero the value is directly used as a seed. 3) equal to zero the machine time fraction of second (uint32_t in nano seconds) is used as a seed. " type="s32" init-value="0" is-not-null="yes" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" /> <attribute name="comment" description="Optional description of this PuDummySteering." type="string" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" multi-value-implementation="list" init-value="" is-not-null="no" /> <relationship name="steps" description="The algorithm steps which will be sequentially executed until an algorithm rejects the event or all steps accept the event." class-type="DummyStep" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" multi-value-implementation="list" /> </class> </oks-schema>

<oks-schema> <info name="" type="" num-of-items="13" oks-format="schema" oks-version="oks-06-10-14 built "Apr 3 2019"" created-by="akazarov" created-on="sunatdaq02" creation-time="20020405T160432" last-modified-by="akazarov" last-modified-on="pc-tbed-pub-28.cern.ch" last-modification-time="20190403T162734" /> <include> <file path="daq/schema/core.schema.xml" /> </include> <class name="Executable" description="Describes a program that is executed on a host with some

Tests with the "any" scope set are always executed.
" type="enum" range="any,precondition,functional,diagnostics" is-multi-value="yes" init-value="any" is-not-null="yes" format="dec" /> <attribute name="Complexity" description="Define level of complexity of test.
When testing of a component is requested with the level 
specified, only those tests with a complexity <= the specified 
level are executed.
If no specific level is requested, all tests are executed." type="u8" range="0,1,2,3" init-value="0" is-not-null="yes" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" /> <attribute name="Validity" description="Amount of seconds during which a test result is valid.
This attribute is used by hte TM client library to avoid useless repetition of tests." type="s32" init-value="60" is-not-null="yes" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" /> <attribute name="RepeatIfUnresolved" description="If set to true a test which results in and UNRESOLVED code will be

in this relationship will have run successfully." class-type="Test" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="ExecDependsOnFailure" description="The test will only be executed once the tests listed

If this relation is left empty, a test failure will
not provide any hint on how to understand/debug/fix the problem." class-type="TestFailure" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> </class> <class name="Test4CORBAServant" description="" is-abstract="no"> <superclass name="Test" /> <attribute name="ServantName" description="Name with which the servant is registered in IPC." type="string" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" init-value="" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="ServantType" description="Type with which the servant is registered in IPC." type="string" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" init-value="" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="ClassName" description="Class of components to which this test applies to." type="class" is-multi-value="yes" init-value="IPCServiceApplicationBase" is-not-null="yes" range="" format="dec" /> <attribute name="CPartitionName" description="Partition in which the Corba Servants are." type="string" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" init-value="" is-not-null="no" /> </class> <class name="Test4Class" description="Describes tests which are applied for all instances of a particular class in the configuration.
" is-abstract="no"> <superclass name="ExecutableTest" /> <attribute name="ClassName" description="Class name from the databse. The test tests all objects of this class." type="class" init-value="Test4Class" is-not-null="yes" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" /> </class> <class name="Test4Object" description="Describes tests which are applied to a set of specific objects in the configuration.
" is-abstract="no"> <superclass name="ExecutableTest" /> <attribute name="OverrideTest4Class" description="Both Test4Class and Test4Object can be defined for an object in database.
If this attribute set ti 'true', Test4Object overrides Test4Class (this is default behaviour).

Objects must belong to classes inherited from TestableObject." class-type="TestableObject" low-cc="one" high-cc="many" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> </class> <class name="TestBehavior" description="This class describes the behavior to adopt when testing a set of 
 objects belonging to the same relationship of a class. Objects linked 
 via this relationship will be tested according to the specified behavior." is-abstract="no"> <attribute name="RelationshipName" description="Name of the Relationship to be followed in a class.
 " type="string" is-not-null="yes" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" init-value="" /> <attribute name="SynchronousTesting" description="Defines whether object should be tested synchronously or in parallel." type="bool" init-value="true" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="StopOnError" description="Determines whether at the first failing test the test sequence shall be interrupted" type="bool" init-value="false" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="IgnoreClasses" description="Object castable to these classes will not be loaded when following this relationship" type="class" is-multi-value="yes" range="" format="dec" init-value="" is-not-null="no" /> </class> <class name="TestFailure" description="Describes a specific failure mode for a Test.

Parameters are to be parsed by the client." type="string" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" init-value="" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="timeout" description="Timeout in seconds for the action to be executed and further actions like test to be performed. " type="u32" init-value="0" range="" format="dec" is-multi-value="no" is-not-null="no" /> <attribute name="description" description="Just a description of an action, to be displayed to a user." example.caption: The public OKS C++ API expressed in the OKS schema format: OksKernel, OksFile, OksClass, OksAttribute, OksRelationship, OksMethod, OksObject, OksData, OksIndex, OksQuery and the whole expression hierarchy (OksComparator, OksRelationshipExpression, OksNotExpression, OksAndExpression, OksOrExpression), plus QueryPath, OksRepositoryVersion and the error taxonomy. C++ data members appear as attributes, associations as relationships, and every documented public method as a method element carrying its verbatim prototype. This is what makes 'which call executes a parsed query?' answerable from the same index as 'which applications run on hostA?'. [Source: docs/OKS_Grammar_Query_CppAPI_Reference.pdf]

Backs the run/revision resolver."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="std::vector<OksRepositoryVersion> get_repository_versions_by_hash(bool skip_irrelevant = true, const std::string& sha1 = "", const std::string& sha2 = "")" body="" /> </method> <method name="get_repository_versions_by_date" description="List repository versions in a date interval."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="std::vector<OksRepositoryVersion> get_repository_versions_by_date(bool skip_irrelevant = true, const std::string& since = "", const std::string& until = "")" body="" /> </method> <method name="get_repository_versions_diff" description="Files that differ between two repository revisions. This is the DTD type enumeration and it decides whether a comparison is numeric or lexicographic." type="enum" range="bool,s8,u8,s16,u16,s32,u32,s64,u64,float,double,date,time,string,uid,enum,class" init-value="string" /> <attribute name="range" description="C++ std::string get_range(). Notation 'A,B,C..D,*..F,G..*': literals, closed intervals, open-below and open-above. Spaces are not allowed. An enum attribute must have a non-empty range; bool has the predefined range true,false." type="string" /> <attribute name="format" description="C++ enum Format { Oct = 8, Dec = 10, Hex = 16 }." type="enum" range="dec,hex,oct" init-value="dec" /> <attribute name="is_multi_value" description="C++ bool get_is_multi_values(). A multi-value attribute holds a list, so a comparison tests the elements." type="bool" init-value="false" /> <attribute name="init_value" description="C++ std::string get_init_value(); std::list<std::string> get_init_values() for multi-value. Objects that store no value are evaluated against this." type="string" /> <attribute name="is_not_null" description="C++ bool get_is_no_null()." type="bool" init-value="false" /> <attribute name="ordered" description="C++ bool. Collection ordering for multi-value attributes." type="bool" init-value="false" /> <relationship name="Class" description="The class that declares this attribute; OksClass::source_class(attr) resolves it through inheritance." class-type="OksClass" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <method name="get_enum_index" description="Position of an enumerator inside the range, or -1. Used to validate an enum value before it reaches the query string."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="int get_enum_index(const std::string&) const noexcept" body="" /> </method> <method name="constructor" description="The full constructor used by every oks_utils example, e.g. OksAttribute a("Max Speed", OksAttribute::u16_int_type, false, "", "160", "max speed of car (km/h)", true)."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksAttribute(const std::string& name, const std::string& type, bool is_mv, const std::string& range, const std::string& init_v, const std::string& description, bool no_null, Format format = Dec, OksClass * p = nullptr)" body="" /> </method> </class> <class name="OksRelationship" description="C++ API (include/oks/relationship.hpp). A typed reference from one object to one or many others. A relationship is either a general (weak) reference or a composite (strong) one; a composite reference may be exclusive or shared, and dependent or independent. Deleting every composite parent deletes a dependent child."> <attribute name="name" description="C++ std::string get_name()." type="string" is-not-null="yes" /> <attribute name="description" description="C++ std::string get_description()." type="string" /> <attribute name="class_type" description="C++ std::string get_type(); OksClass * get_class_type(). The class of the referenced objects, and therefore the class against which a nested relationship expression is parsed." type="string" is-not-null="yes" /> <attribute name="low_cardinality_constraint" description="C++ enum CardinalityConstraint { Zero, One, Many }, low end." type="enum" range="Zero,One,Many" init-value="Zero" /> <attribute name="high_cardinality_constraint" description="C++ enum CardinalityConstraint, high end. 'Many' is what makes the some/all quantifier meaningful." type="enum" range="Zero,One,Many" init-value="One" /> <attribute name="is_composite" description="C++ bool get_is_composite(). A composite (strong) reference owns its target." type="bool" init-value="false" /> <attribute name="is_exclusive" description="C++ bool get_is_exclusive(). An exclusive component belongs to exactly one composite parent." type="bool" init-value="false" /> <attribute name="is_dependent" description="C++ bool get_is_dependent(). A dependent child is destroyed with its last composite parent." type="bool" init-value="false" /> <attribute name="ordered" description="C++ bool. Whether the reference list preserves order." type="bool" init-value="false" /> <relationship name="Class" description="The class that declares this relationship." class-type="OksClass" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="TargetClass" description="get_class_type() resolved to the referenced OksClass." class-type="OksClass" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <method name="constructor" description="Example from oks_utils/examples/relationship.cpp: OksRelationship r("consists of", "Element", OksRelationship::Zero, OksRelationship::Many, true, true, true, false, "A structure consists of zero or many elements")."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksRelationship(const std::string& name, const std::string& type, CardinalityConstraint low_cc, CardinalityConstraint high_cc, bool composite, bool exclusive, bool dependent, const std::string& description, OksClass * p = nullptr)" body="" /> </method> </class> <class name="OksMethod" description="C++ API (include/oks/method.hpp). A named algorithm attached to a schema class, carrying one implementation per language. DAL generates typed accessors from these."> <attribute name="name" description="C++ std::string get_name()." type="string" is-not-null="yes" /> <attribute name="description" description="C++ std::string get_description()." type="string" /> <relationship name="Implementations" description="One entry per language." class-type="OksMethodImplementation" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="yes" is-exclusive="yes" is-dependent="yes" /> <method name="add_implementation" description="Example from oks_utils/examples/method.cpp: m.add_implementation("c++", "void print(const char * s)", "std::cout << s << std::endl;")."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="void add_implementation(const std::string& language, const std::string& prototype, const std::string& body)" body="" /> </method> </class> <class name="OksMethodImplementation" description="C++ API. One language binding of an OksMethod; serialised as the <method-implementation> element of the schema DTD."> <attribute name="language" description="C++ std::string, e.g. c++, c, java." type="string" is-not-null="yes" /> <attribute name="prototype" description="C++ std::string: the declaration." type="string" is-not-null="yes" /> <attribute name="body" description="C++ std::string: the implementation text." type="string" /> </class> <class name="OksObject" description="C++ API (include/oks/object.hpp). One instance: a class, a unique object id, attribute values and relationship references. SatisfiesQueryExpression() is the per-object predicate the query engine evaluates, and find_path() runs a path query."> <attribute name="id" description="C++ std::string GetId(). The object id compared by the (object-id "ID" =) query term. An id lookup is cheaper than a non-indexed attribute scan and works for objects with no searchable attributes." type="string" is-not-null="yes" /> <attribute name="int32_id" description="C++ int32_t get_int32_id(): the optional numeric alias." type="s32" init-value="0" /> <relationship name="Class" description="GetClass(): the class this object instantiates." class-type="OksClass" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="File" description="get_file(): the data file that stores this object." class-type="OksFile" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="AttributeValues" description="GetAttributeValue(name) returns the OksData held for each attribute." class-type="OksData" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="yes" is-exclusive="yes" is-dependent="yes" /> <relationship name="ReverseCompositeRels" description="reverse_composite_rels(): the OksRCR entries naming every composite parent of this object." class-type="OksObject" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <method name="SatisfiesQueryExpression" description="Evaluate one query expression against this object. For a comparator with a nil attribute it compares OksData(GetId()), which is how object-id terms work. For a relationship term it walks the reference list; check-all-objects true means every target must match, false means at least one must."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="bool SatisfiesQueryExpression(OksQueryExpression * query_exp) const" body="" /> </method> <method name="find_path" description="Run a path query from this object; returns the list of objects between the start and the destination, or 0 when no path exists."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksObject::List * find_path(const QueryPath& query) const" body="" /> </method> <method name="GetAttributeValue" description="Read one attribute value. Object lookup plus this call is the no-query path for a question that already names an exact object id."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksData * GetAttributeValue(const std::string& name) const" body="" /> </method> <method name="GetRelationshipValue" description="Read the references held by one relationship. This is relationship navigation: start at an object, follow a named link, land on the target."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksData * GetRelationshipValue(const std::string&) const" body="" /> </method> <method name="SetAttributeValue" description="Write one attribute value. Writes belong behind the policy layer, never on the read path."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="void SetAttributeValue(const std::string& name, OksData * data)" body="" /> </method> <method name="references" description="Collect the objects reachable from this one up to a recursion depth, optionally filtered by class."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="void references(OksObject::FSet& refs, unsigned long recursion_depth, bool add_self = false, ClassSet * classes = 0) const" body="" /> </method> </class> <class name="OksData" description="C++ API (include/oks/object.hpp). A discriminated runtime value. Query comparators compare OksData against OksData, which is why a query string writes every value as a quoted token and lets the attribute's type decide the comparison."> <attribute name="type" description="C++ enum OksData::Type." type="enum" range="unknown_type,s8_type,u8_type,s16_type,u16_type,s32_type,u32_type,s64_type,u64_type,float_type,double_type,bool_type,class_type,object_type,date_type,time_type,string_type,list_type,uid_type,uid2_type,enum_type" init-value="unknown_type" /> <attribute name="value" description="C++ union payload, rendered by str()." type="string" /> <method name="SetValues" description="Parse a textual value into this OksData using an attribute's type and range. The parser calls it for every non-regex comparator."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="void SetValues(const char * s, const OksAttribute * a)" body="" /> </method> <method name="check_range" description="Validate the held value against the attribute range."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="void check_range(const OksAttribute * a) const" body="" /> </method> </class> <class name="OksIndex" description="C++ API (include/oks/index.hpp). A sorted multiset of one class's objects keyed on one attribute. OksClass::execute_query() uses it instead of a linear scan when the comparator attribute is indexed, including two-sided lookups for an and/or of two comparators on the same attribute."> <attribute name="attribute_offset" description="C++ size_t: the data slot the index sorts on." type="u32" init-value="0" /> <relationship name="Class" description="The indexed class." class-type="OksClass" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="Attribute" description="The indexed attribute." class-type="OksAttribute" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <method name="FindEqual" description="Indexed '=' lookup."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksObject::List * FindEqual(OksData * d) const" body="" /> </method> <method name="FindGreatEqual" description="Indexed '>=' lookup, as in oks_utils/examples/index.cpp."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksObject::List * FindGreatEqual(OksData * d) const" body="" /> </method> <method name="FindLessEqualAndGreatEqual" description="Indexed closed-interval lookup, used for (and ("A" "lo" >=) ("A" "hi" <=))."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksObject::List * FindLessEqualAndGreatEqual(OksData * d1, OksData * d2) const" body="" /> </method> </class> <class name="OksRepositoryVersion" description="C++ API (include/oks/kernel.hpp). One commit of the git-backed configuration repository: the unit a run number resolves to before any query is executed."> <attribute name="commit_hash" description="C++ std::string m_commit_hash." type="string" /> <attribute name="user" description="C++ std::string m_user." type="string" /> <attribute name="date" description="C++ std::time_t m_date." type="time" /> <attribute name="comment" description="C++ std::string m_comment." type="string" /> <attribute name="files" description="C++ std::vector<std::string> m_files: the files this commit touched." type="string" is-multi-value="yes" /> </class> <class name="OksQuery" description="C++ API (include/oks/query.hpp). A complete query: a scope flag plus one root expression. It can be built programmatically from expression objects or parsed from a query string; good() reports whether the parse succeeded. Streaming it back out prints the canonical (all|this (<expr>)) form."> <attribute name="search_in_subclasses" description="C++ bool search_in_subclasses(). True is the 'all' scope token, false is 'this'. This is the OksQuery(bool b, ...) first constructor argument." type="bool" init-value="true" /> <attribute name="status" description="C++ int p_status, surfaced by good(). Non-zero means the string failed to parse and the query must not be executed." type="s32" init-value="0" /> <attribute name="query_type" description="C++ enum QueryType, the tag on every expression node." type="enum" range="unknown_type,comparator_type,relationship_type,not_type,and_type,or_type" init-value="unknown_type" /> <attribute name="reserved_tokens" description="C++ static const char * members: OR="or", AND="and", NOT="not", SOME="some", THIS_CLASS="this", ALL_SUBCLASSES="all", OID="object-id", PATH_TO="path-to", DIRECT="direct", NESTED="nested". These are the only structural keywords in the grammar." type="string" is-multi-value="yes" init-value="or,and,not,some,this,all,object-id,path-to,direct,nested" /> <attribute name="comparators" description="C++ static comparator function pointers: equal_cmp '=', not_equal_cmp '!=', reg_exp_cmp '~=', less_or_equal_cmp '<=', greater_or_equal_cmp '>=', less_cmp '<', greater_cmp '>'. reg_exp_cmp uses boost::regex_match, so '~=' matches the whole value." type="string" is-multi-value="yes" init-value="=,!=,~=,<=,>=,<,>" /> <relationship name="Expression" description="get()/set(): the single root expression. The parser rejects a query whose first token is neither 'all' nor 'this'." class-type="OksQueryExpression" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="yes" is-exclusive="yes" is-dependent="yes" /> <method name="parse_constructor" description="Parse a query string against a class. Every attribute, relationship and enum value in the string is resolved through that class, so an unknown name fails here rather than at execution time."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksQuery(const OksClass * c, const std::string& query_string)" body="" /> </method> <method name="build_constructor" description="Build a query from an already-constructed expression tree, e.g. OksQuery q(false, new OksComparator(a, new OksData((unsigned short)200), OksQuery::greater_cmp))."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksQuery(bool search_in_subclasses, OksQueryExpression * q = 0)" body="" /> </method> <method name="good" description="Whether the query parsed. oks_dump checks q->good() before calling execute_query and exits with code 3 when it is false."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="bool good() const" body="" /> </method> </class> <class name="OksQueryExpression" description="C++ API (include/oks/query.hpp). The abstract base of every query node. CheckSyntax() enforces the structural rules the IR validator mirrors: and/or need two or more operands, not needs exactly one, a relationship node needs a nested expression." is-abstract="yes"> <attribute name="type" description="C++ OksQuery::QueryType type()." type="enum" range="unknown_type,comparator_type,relationship_type,not_type,and_type,or_type" init-value="unknown_type" /> <method name="CheckSyntax" description="Structural validation of the node and its children. OksClass::execute_query refuses to run when it returns false."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="bool CheckSyntax() const" body="" /> </method> </class> <class name="OksComparator" description="C++ API. The leaf node of the grammar: an attribute, a value and a comparator function. Serialises as ("attr-name" "value" op). When the attribute pointer is null the node is an object-id test and serialises as (object-id "ID" =)."> <attribute name="comparator_function" description="C++ OksQuery::Comparator: one of equal_cmp, not_equal_cmp, reg_exp_cmp, less_cmp, less_or_equal_cmp, greater_cmp, greater_or_equal_cmp." type="enum" range="equal_cmp,not_equal_cmp,reg_exp_cmp,less_cmp,less_or_equal_cmp,greater_cmp,greater_or_equal_cmp" init-value="equal_cmp" /> <attribute name="is_object_id_test" description="Derived: true when GetAttribute() is null, i.e. the node compares the object id instead of an attribute." type="bool" init-value="false" /> <relationship name="Base" description="Derives from OksQueryExpression with type comparator_type." class-type="OksQueryExpression" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="Attribute" description="GetAttribute(): the attribute under test, or null for an object-id test." class-type="OksAttribute" low-cc="zero" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="Value" description="GetValue(): the OksData compared against. For '~=' it is held as string_type and lazily compiled into a boost::regex." class-type="OksData" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="yes" is-exclusive="yes" is-dependent="yes" /> <method name="constructor" description="Example from oks_utils/examples/comparator.cpp: OksComparator qc(&a, new OksData("Peter"), OksQuery::equal_cmp)."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksComparator(const OksAttribute * a, OksData * v, OksQuery::Comparator f)" body="" /> </method> </class> <class name="OksRelationshipExpression" description="C++ API. A relationship term: follow a named relationship and evaluate the nested expression on the referenced objects. Serialises as ("rel-name" some <expr>) or ("rel-name" all <expr>). The parser types the nested expression against the relationship's target class."> <attribute name="is_check_all_objects" description="C++ bool IsCheckAllObjects(). True is the 'all' quantifier (every referenced object must satisfy the nested expression); false is 'some' (at least one must)." type="bool" init-value="false" /> <relationship name="Base" description="Derives from OksQueryExpression with type relationship_type." class-type="OksQueryExpression" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="Relationship" description="GetRelationship(): the link that is followed." class-type="OksRelationship" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="NestedExpression" description="get(): the expression evaluated on each referenced object, not on the original one." class-type="OksQueryExpression" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="yes" is-exclusive="yes" is-dependent="yes" /> <method name="constructor" description="Example from oks_utils/examples/r_expression.cpp: OksRelationshipExpression rqe(&r, new OksComparator(&a, new OksData("BMW"), OksQuery::equal_cmp), false)."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksRelationshipExpression(const OksRelationship * r, OksQueryExpression * q, bool check_all_objects = false)" body="" /> </method> </class> <class name="OksNotExpression" description="C++ API. Logical negation. Serialises as (not <expr>) and takes exactly one operand; the parser rejects any other count."> <relationship name="Base" description="Derives from OksQueryExpression with type not_type." class-type="OksQueryExpression" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="Operand" description="get(): the single negated expression." class-type="OksQueryExpression" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="yes" is-exclusive="yes" is-dependent="yes" /> <method name="constructor" description="Example from oks_utils/examples/not_expression.cpp: OksNotExpression ne(new OksComparator(&a, new OksData((unsigned short)25), OksQuery::less_cmp))."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="OksNotExpression(OksQueryExpression * q = 0)" body="" /> </method> </class> <class name="OksListBaseQueryExpression" description="C++ API. The shared operand list behind the and/or nodes." is-abstract="yes"> <relationship name="Operands" description="expressions(): the operand list; add() appends." class-type="OksQueryExpression" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="yes" is-exclusive="yes" is-dependent="yes" /> </class> <class name="OksAndExpression" description="C++ API. Logical conjunction, serialised as (and e1 e2 ...). The parser requires two or more operands. Example from oks_utils/examples/and_expression.cpp: a closed interval 60 <= weight <= 90 built from a greater_or_equal_cmp and a less_or_equal_cmp on the same attribute."> <relationship name="Base" description="Derives from OksQueryExpression with type and_type." class-type="OksQueryExpression" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="OperandList" description="Derives from OksListBaseQueryExpression." class-type="OksListBaseQueryExpression" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> </class> <class name="OksOrExpression" description="C++ API. Logical disjunction, serialised as (or e1 e2 ...). The parser requires two or more operands. Example from oks_utils/examples/or_expression.cpp: tall or short, two comparators on the same float attribute."> <relationship name="Base" description="Derives from OksQueryExpression with type or_type." class-type="OksQueryExpression" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="OperandList" description="Derives from OksListBaseQueryExpression." class-type="OksListBaseQueryExpression" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> </class> <class name="QueryPath" description="C++ API (oks::QueryPath, include/oks/query.hpp). A path query: (path-to "id@class" <path-expression>). The destination is written id@class and must resolve to a loaded object; an unparseable path throws oks::bad_query_syntax. Path queries describe topology and are not attribute filters, which is why the IR used by the translator cannot express them today."> <attribute name="destination" description="C++: parsed out of the quoted "object-id@class-name" token; the class is resolved with kernel.find_class() and the object with OksClass::get_object()." type="string" is-not-null="yes" /> <relationship name="GoalObject" description="get_goal_object(): the object the path must reach." class-type="OksObject" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no" is-exclusive="no" is-dependent="no" /> <relationship name="StartExpression" description="get_start_expression(): the first (direct ...) or (nested ...) step." class-type="QueryPathExpression" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="yes" is-exclusive="yes" is-dependent="yes" /> <method name="constructor" description="Parse a path query. Example: (path-to "my-id@my-class" (direct "A" "B" (nested "N" (direct "X" "Y" "Z"))))."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="QueryPath(const std::string& query, const OksKernel& kernel)" body="" /> </method> </class> <class name="QueryPathExpression" description="C++ API. One step of a path query: a traversal mode plus a list of quoted relationship names plus an optional next step. 'direct' follows the named relationships once; 'nested' looks through recursively nested objects. Relationship names must be quoted."> <attribute name="use_nested_lookup" description="C++ bool get_use_nested_lookup(): true for the 'nested' keyword, false for 'direct'." type="bool" init-value="false" /> <attribute name="rel_names" description="C++ std::list<std::string> get_rel_names(): the relationships followed at this step." type="string" is-multi-value="yes" /> <relationship name="Next" description="get_next(): the nested step, which is what makes a path query multi-level." class-type="QueryPathExpression" low-cc="zero" high-cc="one" is-composite="yes" is-exclusive="yes" is-dependent="yes" /> </class> <class name="OksException" description="C++ API (include/oks/exceptions.hpp and query.hpp). The failure taxonomy a generated query can hit. Each value maps to a distinct repair action, which is why the error breakdown is reported per category rather than as a single pass/fail number."> <attribute name="kind" description="C++ exception types thrown on the query path." type="enum" range="bad_query_syntax,BadReqExp,QueryFailed,AttributeReadError,FailedLoadFile,FailedSaveFile" init-value="bad_query_syntax" /> <attribute name="oks_dump_exit_code" description="Exit status of the oks_dump validation oracle: 0 success, 1 bad command line, 2 bad OKS file, 3 bad query, 4 no such class, 5 dangling references, 6 exception caught." type="enum" range="0,1,2,3,4,5,6" init-value="0" /> <attribute name="what" description="C++ const char * what()." type="string" /> </class> </oks-schema>

example.caption: Concrete objects from the ATLAS TDAQ test configuration: 75 object(s) in common-environment.data.xml. Object ids are what an (object-id "ID" =) term compares against, so these blocks ground entity resolution as well as schema retrieval. [Source: test_data/segments/common-environment.data.xml]

[Sources: https://github.com/DUNE-DAQ/dal - schema/dal/tutorial.schema.xml, scripts/dal_testing.data.xml]

example.caption: The ATLAS/TDAQ core schema (real production classes). The run-level entry point is the Partition: it holds top-level Segments, the online infrastructure, disabled components, tags, parameters and (important) the database attributes DBPath/DBName/DBVersion — DBVersion is the OKS git SHA used for the partition, i.e. the answer to "what configuration was used". Methods get_config_version()/set_config_version() are the DAL interface for that. Also shows the C++/Java dual-language method bodies typical of dal-generated code. [Source: https://github.com/DUNE-DAQ/dal - schema/dal/core.schema.xml]
example.schema-file: <class name="Partition" description="The class describes TDAQ configuration including top-level segments, disabled components, various TDAQ base and user specific parameters."> <attribute name="RepositoryRoot" description="Temporary sw installation area having highest priority" type="string"/> <attribute name="IPCRef" description="IPC init reference; default from TDAQ_IPC_INIT_REF env" type="string" init-value="$(TDAQ_IPC_INIT_REF)"/> <attribute name="DBPath" description="Locations of database repositories (OKS_DB_ROOT); default from TDAQ_DB_PATH" type="string" init-value="$(TDAQ_DB_PATH)"/> <attribute name="DBName" description="Name of the OKS data file; default from TDAQ_DB_DATA" type="string" init-value="$(TDAQ_DB_DATA)"/> <attribute name="DBVersion" description="Database version (SHA key) if GIT repository is used; default from TDAQ_DB_VERSION" type="string" init-value="$(TDAQ_DB_VERSION)"/> <attribute name="DBTechnology" description="Config database technology implementation" type="enum" range="rdbconfig,oksconflibs" init-value="rdbconfig"/> <attribute name="RunTypes" type="string" is-multi-value="yes"/> <relationship name="Segments" description="Top-level segments composing given partition. To disable a segment, add it to Disabled instead of removing it." class-type="Segment" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="yes"/> <relationship name="OnlineInfrastructure" description="Defines online infrastructure segment." class-type="OnlineSegment" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no"/> <relationship name="Disabled" description="Lists segments and resources which are temporary disabled." class-type="Component" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="no" ordered="yes"/> <relationship name="DefaultHost" description="Host to run all applications with empty 'RunsOn'." class-type="Computer" low-cc="zero" high-cc="one" is-composite="no"/> <relationship name="DefaultTags" description="Default tags used to select binaries for applications without explicit tag." class-type="Tag" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="no"/> <relationship name="ProcessEnvironment" description="Process environment for any application ran in given partition." class-type="Parameter" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="no"/> <method name="set_config_version" description="Set configuration version, i.e. OKS GIT repository SHA. The partition infrastructure has to be running."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="void set_config_version(const std::string& name, bool reload) const"/> <method-implementation language="java" prototype="void set_config_version(final String version, boolean reload) throws config.GenericException, config.SystemException, config.NotFoundException, config.NotValidException"/> </method> <method name="get_config_version" description="Return configuration version used by given partition, i.e. OKS GIT repository SHA. The partition infrastructure has to be running."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="std::string get_config_version() const"/> <method-implementation language="java" prototype="String get_config_version() throws config.GenericException, config.SystemException, config.NotFoundException, config.NotValidException"/> </method> </class>

example.caption: The OKS data type reference (CERN oks repo test): all attribute types (bool..u64, float, double, date, time, string, enum, class), multi-value attributes, hex format, and the compact "data" format (attr val inside tag). Good grounding for translating attribute names to type-correct query values. [Sources: https://gitlab.cern.ch/atlas-tdaq-software/oks - test/all_types.schema.xml, test/test.data.xml]
example.schema-file: <oks-schema> <class name="Element" description="It is a class to describe a person"> <attribute name="Boolean" type="bool"/> <attribute name="IntS8" type="s8"/> <attribute name="IntU8" type="u8"/> <attribute name="IntS16" type="s16"/> <attribute name="IntU16" type="u16"/> <attribute name="IntS32" type="s32"/> <attribute name="IntU32" type="u32"/> <attribute name="IntS64" type="s64"/> <attribute name="Int64" type="u64"/> <attribute name="Float" type="float"/> <attribute name="Double" type="double"/> <attribute name="String" type="string"/> <attribute name="Date" type="date"/> <attribute name="Time" type="time"/> <attribute name="Enum" type="enum" range="one,two,three,four,five" init-value="one"/> <attribute name="Class" type="class" init-value="Container"/> <attribute name="ArrayIntS8" type="s8" is-multi-value="yes"/> <attribute name="ArrayString" type="string" is-multi-value="yes"/> <attribute name="ArrayEnum" type="enum" range="one,two,three,four,five" is-multi-value="yes" init-value="one"/> <attribute name="HexIntU8" type="u8" format="hex"/> <attribute name="HexIntU64" type="u64" format="hex"/> </class> </oks-schema>
example.data-file: <oks-data> <include><file path="all_types.schema.xml"/></include> <obj class="Element" id="o1-good"> <attr name="Boolean" type="bool" val="1"/> <attr name="IntS8" type="s8" val="-128"/> <attr name="IntU16" type="u16" val="50000"/> <attr name="IntS64" type="s64" val="-10000000000"/> <attr name="Float" type="float" val="3.1415"/> <attr name="Double" type="double" val="2.1928"/> <attr name="String" type="string" val="The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."/> <attr name="Date" type="date" val="20240809"/> <attr name="Time" type="time" val="20240809T150647"/> <attr name="Enum" type="enum" val="one"/> <attr name="Class" type="class" val="Container"/> <attr name="ArrayIntS8" type="s8"> <data val="1"/> <data val="-1"/> <data val="127"/> </attr> <attr name="HexIntU8" type="u8" val="0xff"/> <attr name="HexIntU64" type="u64" val="0x123456789abcdef"/> </obj> <obj class="Container" id="o1-good-container"> <attr name="Date" type="date" val="20240829"/> <attr name="Time" type="time" val="20240829T104831"/> <attr name="Enum" type="enum" val="one"/> <attr name="Class" type="class" val="Container"/> <rel name="Root" class="Element" id="o1-good"/> <rel name="Contains"> <ref class="Element" id="o1-good"/> </rel> </obj> </oks-data>

example.caption: Classic DAQ configuration classes (oks_utils tests): software objects, computers, programs, environment variables and the (dynamic) Process class. Shows the old naming conventions still used in production DBs. [Source: https://gitlab.cern.ch/atlas-tdaq-software/oks_utils - tests/DAQ-Configuration.schema.xml]
example.schema-file: <oks-schema> <class name="Computer" description="Describes an abstract computer."> <attribute name="Name" description="Computer name (e.g. pc-tdaq-onl-01)" type="string" is-not-null="yes"/> <attribute name="OSType" description="Operating system type" type="enum" range="Linux,SunOS,Win32"/> <attribute name="CPUSpeed" description="CPU speed in MHz" type="u16"/> </class> <class name="Environment" description="The Environment class is used to describe environment variables and their values. These variables are defined and values are assigned before starting the corresponding process."> <attribute name="Name" type="string" is-not-null="yes"/> <attribute name="Value" type="string"/> </class> <class name="Program" description="This class is used to describe platform dependent part of DAQ software component. It defines default parameters to start a program (command line, environment, priority, etc.)."> <attribute name="CommandLine" type="string"/> <attribute name="Priority" type="s32" init-value="0"/> </class> <class name="Process" description="The Process class is used to describe a dynamic physical part of a software object: logical name of the process, process id, date and time of start, real process priority and privileges."> <attribute name="Id" type="string" is-not-null="yes"/> <attribute name="StartTime" type="time"/> <relationship name="Program" class-type="Program" low-cc="one" high-cc="one"/> <relationship name="RunsOn" class-type="Computer" low-cc="one" high-cc="one"/> </class> </oks-schema>

example.caption: The oks2coral archiving schema: ConfigVersions records which archive (schema/data version) of the OKS database was used for a given run — the offline counterpart of the online "r380689@all_hosts" git tags. [Source: https://gitlab.cern.ch/atlas-tdaq-software/oks2coral - data/oks-archive-info.xml]
example.schema-file: <oks-schema> <class name="ConfigVersions" description="The class is used to store archive versions of the OKS database used for given run."> <superclass name="Info"/> <attribute name="Run" type="u32" is-not-null="yes" init-value="0"/> <attribute name="SchemaVersion" type="u32" init-value="0"/> <attribute name="DataVersion" type="u32" init-value="0"/> <attribute name="TotalVersion" type="string"/> <attribute name="Time" type="time" init-value="11-10"/> </class> </oks-schema>
